title: Add synthetic failover canary scenario for partial regional impairment + recovery time reporting
author: Caleb Johnson
body:
Context
We’re validating the Regional failover automation upgrade with controlled tests (game days + low-risk prod slices). The existing perf-canary suite covers basic “hard down” failover, but we were missing a realistic partial-impairment scenario (e.g., packet loss / elevated tail latency) where the platform is expected to enter a degraded state first and recover without a full failover in some cases.

This PR adds a new synthetic failover canary scenario that simulates partial regional impairment and records recovery metrics so we can quantify:
- time-to-detect (TTD) from impairment start
- time-to-mitigate (TTM) until error/latency returns under thresholds
- time-to-recover (TTR) until region health stabilizes (hysteresis window satisfied)

What’s in this PR
- New scenario: partial_regional_impairment
  - Generates steady synthetic traffic against a chosen {region, route, model} tuple
  - Induces impairment using an environment-specific “fault injector” mechanism
    - staging: netem-based packet loss/latency on the regional edge canary target
    - prod: disabled by default; requires allowlist + explicit --enable-prod-faults flag
  - Observes platform behavior (error rate + p95/p99 + stream disconnects) and region-health signal outputs
- Metrics/reporting
  - Emits Prometheus metrics for each run:
    - perf_canary_failover_ttd_seconds{scenario,region}
    - perf_canary_failover_ttm_seconds{scenario,region}
    - perf_canary_failover_ttr_seconds{scenario,region}
    - perf_canary_failover_peak_5xx_rate{scenario,region}
    - perf_canary_failover_peak_p99_ms{scenario,region}
  - Adds a small markdown summary artifact uploaded to CI for easy review (same format used in game day readouts)
- Guardrails
  - Max QPS and token budgets enforced for the scenario (defaults: 0.2 RPS, max_tokens=64)
  - Hard stop conditions:
    - >2 minutes sustained 5xx > 20% (abort + auto-disable fault injection)
    - >5 minutes without entering expected state (abort + mark run failed)
  - Uses hold-down timers in expected-state evaluation to avoid flakey pass/fail on transient recovery

Expected outcomes / acceptance criteria
- staging: a 3-minute impairment should be detected within 90s and the canary should report recovery within 6 minutes after fault removal (including hysteresis window)
- prod (monitor-only dry run): scenario should execute without enabling fault injection and should still compute baseline latency/error metrics

Testing
- Local: go test ./... + scenario runner dry mode
- CI: added integration job to run partial_regional_impairment in staging-like docker env (fault injector mocked)

Notes / follow-ups
- Once trigger engine thresholds are finalized, we should align the canary “expected degraded window” with the SLO burn-rate alert configuration (tracked in ENG-2853).
- This intentionally does not attempt to validate DNS TTL propagation behavior; that’s covered separately in infra/game-day checklists.

Screenshots / sample output
Included in CI artifact: canary-report-partial_regional_impairment.md (see Checks).
commits: canary/scenarios: add partial_regional_impairment scenario skeleton + runner wiring
fault-injector: implement staging netem driver + prod safety gating
metrics: emit TTD/TTM/TTR and peak error/latency gauges
reporting: attach markdown report artifact to CI
ci: add integration job w/ mocked fault injector
conversation: Miles Thornton (review): Can we make sure prod runs cannot enable faults accidentally? I want an explicit allowlist AND an interactive confirmation when running locally.

Caleb Johnson (author): Added two gates: (1) prod enablement requires --enable-prod-faults and an allowlisted region in partial_regional_impairment.prod.yaml; (2) when running with a TTY we require typing the region name to proceed. In CI it will refuse to run with prod faults enabled.
Aisha Bello (review): The TTR definition should account for hysteresis; otherwise this will be noisy. Can we match the trigger engine’s “stable for N minutes” semantics?

Caleb Johnson (author): Updated expected-state evaluation to require stable health for 3 consecutive evaluation windows (configurable). Also added perf_canary_failover_ttr_seconds to start at impairment end and end only when stable window criteria met.
Sergio Costa (review): Please include stream disconnect rate; we’ve seen this be the customer-visible symptom before 5xx spikes.

Caleb Johnson (author): Added metric perf_canary_failover_peak_stream_disconnect_rate and included it in the markdown report. Also updated docs to clarify how we detect streaming disconnects (client-side).
Emily Zhao (review): The netem driver should no-op cleanly on macOS dev machines. Right now it errors.
Caleb Johnson (author): Good catch—netem is now linux-only with a clear warning + automatic fallback to dry-run mode on unsupported platforms.
Miles Thornton (approval): Looks good. Guardrails are strong enough for staging game day usage.
Aisha Bello (approval): Approved once the metrics names match our conventions—thanks for adding stable-window handling.
Sergio Costa (approval): Report artifact is helpful; ship it.
release_notes: perf-canary: new partial regional impairment failover canary scenario with recovery time metrics and CI report artifact
